The '''7th Academy Awards''', honoring the [[1934 in film|best films for 1934]], was held on February 27, 1935,<ref>{{cite web |last1=Feinberg |first1=Scott |title=Oscars: How One Nominee Found Herself at a Train Station on the Night of the 7th Awards |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/oscars-how-one-nominee-found-herself-at-union-station-on-the-night-of-the-7th-awards-4171293/ |website=The Hollywood Reporter |access-date=23 January 2024 |date=23 April 2021}}</ref> at the [[Millennium Biltmore Hotel|Biltmore Hotel]] in [[Los Angeles]], California. They were hosted by [[Irvin S. Cobb]]. Since this ceremony, the [[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences|Academy]]'s award eligibility period coincided with the calendar year (with temporary exceptions for the [[93rd Academy Awards|93rd]] and [[94th Academy Awards]] due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]).

[[Frank Capra]]'s influential [[romantic comedy]] ''[[It Happened One Night]]'' became the first of three films to date to [[List of Big Five Academy Award winners and nominees|"sweep" the top five awards]]: [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]], [[Academy Award for Best Director|Best Director]], [[Academy Award for Best Actor|Best Actor]], [[Academy Award for Best Actress|Best Actress]], and [[Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay|Best Screenplay]]. This feat would later be matched by ''[[One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest (film)|One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest]]'' in [[48th Academy Awards|1975]] and ''[[The Silence of the Lambs (film)|The Silence of the Lambs]]'' in [[64th Academy Awards|1991]]. It also was the first romantic comedy to win Best Picture, and the first film to win two acting Oscars as well as the first film to win more than 3 awards.

The categories of [[Academy Award for Best Film Editing|Best Film Editing]], [[Academy Award for Best Original Score|Best Original Score]], and [[Academy Award for Best Original Song|Best Original Song]] were introduced this year. This was the first of only two years in which [[write-in candidate]]s were permitted, a response to a controversy surrounding [[Bette Davis]] not being nominated for her role in ''[[Of Human Bondage (1934 film)|Of Human Bondage]]''.<ref name="Oscars '34 Notes">{{cite book |last1=Wallechinsky |first1=David |last2=Wallace |first2=Irving |date=1975 |title=The People's Almanac |url=https://archive.org/details/peoplesalmanac00wall/page/832/mode/2up |location=Garden City, New York |publisher=Doubleday & Company, Inc. |page=833 |isbn=0-385-04060-1}}</ref> The Academy, inundated by calls, letters and editorials decrying this slight, told members they could vote in names on a printed ballot or write in any other name that was desired. [[Claudette Colbert]] declared that this announcement would give Davis the win in a walk.<ref name="Oscars '34 Notes"/> However, in final voting, Davis came in fourth place. Colbert, who viewed herself as having no chance, was informed of her victory upon boarding a train for New York. She hastily rushed into the ceremony to collect her award, then went back to the waiting train.<ref name="Oscars '34 Notes"/>  

This was the last time that all Best Actor nominees were first time acting nominees until the [[95th Academy Awards]], and the last time until the [[43rd Academy Awards]] where either lead acting category was entirely first-time nominees.

Six-year-old [[Shirley Temple]] received the first [[Academy Juvenile Award|Juvenile Award]], making her the [[List of oldest and youngest Academy Award winners and nominees|youngest Oscar recipient]]. [[Clark Gable]] was the first Best Actor winner born in the 20th century (1901).

=== Special Award ===

* To [[Shirley Temple]], in grateful recognition of her outstanding contribution to screen entertainment during the year 1934.
